notes: Biogen paid $7.3B for Reata's Skyclarys (omaveloxolone) — a Nrf2 activator for Friedreich's ataxia (rare neurodegenerative disease). Asset was already FDA-approved (Feb 2023) at deal time. EV/peak-sales reflects an asset post-de-risking. Strong rare-disease ultra-orphan economics with effective monopoly.
selection_rationale: Recent (2023), single-asset, CNS-small-molecule M&A. Important counterpoint to the Karuna and Cerevel deals: Reata was post-approval (less risk → lower multiple) vs Karuna (NDA stage) and Cerevel (Phase 2). Including all three gives the framework a calibrated range for pre- vs post-de-risking CNS valuations.
source: Biogen press release Jul 28 2023; Reata 8-K filing; FDA approval letter Feb 28 2023.
